name: sol_basics_vi_svi_19
description: Solidity 0.6.9 bug: internal library calldata params via `using for` read invalid data
question: The source file in `source` declares `pragma solidity 0.6.9;` (or another version affected by this bug) and defines or uses an internal library function that takes a `calldata` parameter, invoked on a type via a `using ... for` directive, such that invalid or corrupted data can be read at runtime due to the compiler bug, excluding cases where the library functions only take `memory`/`storage`/value-type parameters or the file targets a fixed, unaffected Solidity version.
criteria: A library defines `function foo(bytes calldata data) internal` and the contract has `using MyLib for bytes;` then calls `data.foo()` on a calldata bytes variable
pragma solidity 0.6.9; combined with a library internal function signature like `function process(uint256[] calldata arr) internal pure returns (...)` attached via `using Lib for uint256[];`
An internal library function with a `calldata` struct parameter is bound with `using StructLib for MyStruct;` and invoked as `myStructVar.libFunc()` within a 0.6.9-pragma file
A library exposes multiple internal functions taking `calldata` arrays/structs, all attached via `using` directives and called throughout the contract under the 0.6.9 pragma
